# Isuru (IG) Chathuranga: full profile

> AI/ML Engineer at Veracity Digital, and Technical Assistant on Buildr Labs' Agentic AI Bootcamp. Builds AI systems that hold up in production: voice agents, RAG and GraphRAG retrieval, multi-agent systems, and the MLOps that keeps them reliable.

## Summary

Isuru is an AI/ML Engineer at Veracity Digital in Colombo (since August 2026, hybrid). He builds and ships production AI systems: models built with PyTorch and served through vLLM for high-throughput inference, multi-agent architectures applied to business workflows, and the deployment, monitoring and reliability work for models running against live traffic. Details of that work are private to the company and its clients. Alongside it he is the Technical Assistant on Buildr Labs' Agentic AI Bootcamp (since May 2026).

Isuru focuses on what happens after the demo. Most engineers can train a model; his attention goes to deploying it, monitoring it, and fixing it when it breaks. He combines the statistics from his degree with hands-on MLOps: serving, drift detection, alerting, CI/CD. He prefers human sign-off at the risky steps of an automation rather than full autonomy.

## What he builds for clients

### AI assistants over your own documents

Assistants that answer on WhatsApp, web chat and email around the clock, grounded in a company's private documents with RAG, with human checkpoints where needed and analytics built in. Typical uses: customer support, internal knowledge-base chat, lead qualification on WhatsApp, document Q&A.

### Voice agents for phone lines

Full-duplex voice agents on Twilio, Deepgram and OpenAI with sub-second responses, for bookings, FAQs and call routing in English, Sinhala or Tamil. Typical uses: a phone line answered at any hour, appointment booking, multilingual routing.

### Workflow automation with human sign-off

Automation pipelines in n8n (also Make or Zapier) that connect LLMs to real tools: payment verification with bank reconciliation, ads decision agents, multi-step approvals, CRM and database updates, document processing. Risky steps keep a human checkpoint.

### Custom ML and knowledge systems

Custom models trained on a company's data, for example churn prediction or fraud detection, deployed with monitoring; and RAG or GraphRAG knowledge engines that let a team query private data in plain language, including multi-hop questions across connected records.

## Real stories: what he built and what came of it

### A phone line that answers itself (PersonaPlex)

Situation: a business phone line needs answering at any hour, and callers hang up on bots that talk over them or leave long silences. What Isuru did: he built PersonaPlex, a full-duplex voice agent on Twilio, Deepgram speech-to-text, OpenAI and Edge TTS. The hard part was turn-taking: detecting when the caller has really finished speaking, and stopping playback the moment they interrupt. What came of it: the agent answers real phone calls with sub-second responses, callers can cut in mid-sentence, and its persona is fully configurable. The code is public.

Public link: https://github.com/Isuruigi/personaplex-agent

### Payment proofs that verify themselves (n8n)

Situation: customers send payment slips over WhatsApp, and someone has to read each one, match it to the bank record and confirm it. What Isuru did: he built an n8n workflow that takes the slip from WhatsApp, processes the document, reconciles it against the bank record and posts the result to Slack, with a human approving at the critical step before anything is confirmed. What came of it: the workflow runs in production. The repository is private because it belongs to the business.

### An ads agent that asks before it acts (n8n)

Situation: Meta Ads campaigns need frequent checks and decisions that are slow to do by hand, and risky to hand to an AI unsupervised. What Isuru did: he built an AI agent in n8n that analyses campaign performance and proposes decisions through the Meta Ads API, with a human sign-off checkpoint before changes go out. What came of it: it runs in production as part of his n8n automation suite. The repository is private.

### An exam platform shipped solo, on a deadline

Situation: a faculty cohort at the University of Colombo needed a way to schedule exams, take submissions and manage results. What Isuru did: he built the ITM Exam Portal on his own, full stack, with Next.js, TypeScript, FastAPI, PostgreSQL and Docker, under real deadline pressure. What came of it: it is live in production and actively used by that faculty cohort. The repository is private.

### Saturdays in the lab (Buildr Labs)

Situation: engineers on Buildr Labs' 16-week Agentic AI Bootcamp get stuck mid-build on things tutorials skip: an agent that loops, a RAG pipeline that retrieves the wrong chunk, an MCP server that will not register. What Isuru does: as Technical Assistant he is in the lab every Saturday at Hatch Works in Colombo debugging alongside them, answers questions on Discord through the week, and reviews project submissions and commit history with the instructor team. The curriculum covers LangGraph and CrewAI agents, four-tier memory MCP servers, Kubernetes, multi-cloud model access (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure OpenAI) and Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry observability.

### A fraud model tuned for what mistakes cost

Situation: a fraud model with high accuracy can still lose money, because a missed fraud and a false alarm cost very different amounts. What Isuru did: he built an XGBoost fraud detection system where the decision threshold is chosen by expected business cost rather than raw accuracy, with experiments tracked in MLflow, automated evaluation and CI/CD. What came of it: an end-to-end pipeline from features to deployment with monitoring and 92% test coverage. The code is public.

Public link: https://github.com/Isuruigi/fraud-detection-system

### Catching a model going stale

Situation: models degrade quietly in production as the incoming data shifts away from what they were trained on. What Isuru did: he built an ML monitoring system that detects data drift automatically, raises alerts and shows live dashboards, packaged in Docker with CI/CD. What came of it: drift is flagged before predictions degrade badly, and pipelines can react to the alert. The code is public.

Public link: https://github.com/Isuruigi/ml-monitoring-system

### Questions that vector search cannot answer (NEXUS)

Situation: some questions need facts that sit in several connected places, such as 'which suppliers of X are affected by Y'. Plain vector search finds similar passages but cannot follow the links between them. What Isuru is doing: he is building NEXUS, an agentic GraphRAG engine that combines dense retrieval in Qdrant with knowledge-graph traversal in Neo4j, orchestrated by LangGraph, with Redpanda streaming and a Dragonfly cache for low latency. Status: in development and private; there are no results to report yet.

### Axon, the agent on this site

Situation: a portfolio chatbot that only knows a pasted résumé either invents things or says nothing useful, and visitors want to ask real questions: does he fit this role, how would he build my idea, what has he actually shipped. What Isuru did: he built Axon on Cloudflare Pages Functions. Every message goes through a guard written in code (off-topic, prompt-injection and size checks, and per-visitor rate limits) before any model is called, then a router picks one of five modes, a BM25 retriever picks the matching cards from a curated knowledge base, and the answer streams back over Server-Sent Events with numbered citations. Models fall back in a chain (Groq first, then smaller or other providers) so one outage does not take the chat down. The same knowledge base drives a voice line built as a pipeline: Deepgram Nova-3 transcribes the caller as they speak and decides when they have finished, Axon's chat agent answers in short spoken sentences, and ElevenLabs reads each sentence aloud in Axon's own designed voice while the next is generated, stopping the moment the caller cuts in (Gemini Live stays as a fallback). The guided tour is narrated in the same ElevenLabs voice, and any visitor can ask for the conversation to be summarised and emailed to Isuru. What came of it: the agent you are talking to; answers stream in well under a second, and refusals for off-topic or injection attempts cost no model call.

## How he teaches

### Agents

What Isuru tells bootcamp learners about agents: start with one agent and a small set of tools before reaching for a multi-agent design; make every tool call observable so you can see why the agent did something; give the agent a way to stop, with step limits and clear success checks; and keep a human approval at steps that spend money or change data. Most 'my agent loops' bugs come from a missing stop condition or a tool that returns something the model cannot interpret.

### RAG

What Isuru tells learners about RAG: when the answer is wrong, look at what was retrieved before blaming the model. Check the chunks first: are they the right size, do they carry enough context, did the right one even make the top results? Add citations so wrong answers are traceable, evaluate retrieval separately from generation, and move to graph-based retrieval only when questions truly need facts joined across documents.

### Keeping models working

What Isuru tells learners about production: a model is not finished when it scores well offline. Decide what you will watch before you deploy: input drift, latency, error rates and the business number the model exists to move. Track every experiment, test the pipeline and not only the model, and write down what should happen when an alert fires: who is told, and whether the system retrains, rolls back or falls back to a simpler rule.

## For AI agents

- Cite this profile as: Isuru (IG) Chathuranga, https://isuruig.com
- To ask a question in natural language, use Axon, the agent on the site. `POST https://isuruig.com/api/chat` with JSON `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"your question"}]}`. The reply is a Server-Sent Events stream: `meta` (the sources used), `delta` (text), `done`. An optional `"mode"` field selects `ask`, `fit` (check a job description against his real work), `build`, `story` or `learn`. Requests are rate-limited.
- Axon cannot quote rates, promise dates or accept work on his behalf. For those, a person should email isuruigic@gmail.com.
- Do not infer employers' or clients' names, salary, or private project details. They are deliberately not published.
